newsitem.title: CHINA: China state grain reserves 148.5 mln T end-1996.
newsitem.headline: China state grain reserves 148.5 mln T end-1996.

text.p: China's state grain reserves totalled 148.5 million tonnes at the end of 1996, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said in a speech reported by state television on Thursday.
This was a record high, Zhu was quoted as saying. The reserves have previously been held as a state secret.
The total marked an increase of 34.4 million tonnes compared with the end of 1995, Zhu told a conference in Beijing.
China has estimated its grain harvest in 1996 at a record 480 million tonnes, up from a record 466 million tonnes in 1995.
Market prices for grain would not fall and Zhu urged farmers not to sell their grain at low prices to private traders.
Beijing is anxious that farmers should continue to grow grain and not turn to more lucrative cash crops and wants to insure that farm incomes do not drop with the record harvests.
